title: First local report task (create-only approval, independent checker)
objective: Run the first complete local task through orceld: a planner reads known figures from workspace files the kernel observed and hashed, proposes one report, the user approves exactly that create-only file in the task's folder, orceld creates it, and an independent checker re-reads the saved bytes and confirms the hash and the unchanged sources. Overwrite, out-of-scope and stale-source attempts are refused. Task status and steps are visible through the existing read-only app API. This implements roadmap increment F2 of the adopted plan (docs/orcel/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md) on the F1 approval ledger (#286), the F0 app API (CR-01 #370, #393, #410, #414) and the existing workspace file provider.

include: Activate the SG-000126 contract only; the task model, the report capability, the verifier and the app API methods require separately exact-head qualified implementation PRs.

One new kernel capability `report` with exactly three operations, admitted by orcel-policy and dispatched only by orceld: `report/start` (read-only: validate a title, one to eight workspace-relative UTF-8 source files and one existing workspace-relative output folder; read each source through the existing orcel-provider-fs read path within its limits; record each source's SHA-256 and size; open a task record), `report/preview` (no effect: check a single-component report name and its UTF-8 content against the task, the recorded sources and the folder, and return the exact destination, size and SHA-256 the approval will bind) and `report/commit` (one SOFT approval through the existing broker whose digest binds the workspace, the policy revision, the task id, the folder, the destination, the content SHA-256 and size and every source path and SHA-256; then one create-only write through the existing orcel-provider-fs create path).

Create-only: the destination must not exist at preview, at commit before approval, and at the write itself (the provider's create-new open). An existing destination is refused and is never truncated, replaced, renamed or written; a different name needs a new preview and a new approval.

Scope: the folder must be an existing plain directory inside the workspace (no link, junction or reparse point as its last component) and keep the canonical path recorded at start, and the destination's parent must canonicalize to that path (a folder removed and recreated as a plain directory at the same path counts as the same folder); the report name is one path component of letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', at most 96 characters, not starting with '.', ending in .md, .txt or .csv. Anything else, including separators, '..', drive or UNC prefixes and absolute paths, is refused before any approval.

Staleness: at preview and again at commit (before approval and before the write) every source is re-hashed through the provider and must equal its recorded SHA-256; a changed, missing or replaced source makes the task stale, which is terminal, and a new task must observe the sources again.

Independent checker: after the write, a verifier that shares no code with the writer re-opens the destination with plain std::fs reads, requires a regular file (not a link or reparse point) whose parent is the recorded folder, and checks its size, its SHA-256 against the approved one and every source's SHA-256 against its recorded value. Only a passing check marks the task verified; a failing check is a typed postcondition failure and the file is left in place for the user to inspect. The end-to-end tests add a second checker, in the test harness, that parses the saved report and recomputes the expected figures from the fixture sources itself.

Minimal task records: an in-memory, bounded registry owned by orceld (at most 64 tasks per daemon run; the oldest finished task is evicted first, and start is refused when every slot holds an unfinished task). States: observed, proposed, approval_denied, committing, verified, verification_failed, stale, failed. A denied approval leaves the task open for a fresh commit with a fresh approval; verified, verification_failed, stale and failed are final. There is no cancel: when all 64 slots hold unfinished tasks, start is refused until the daemon restarts (a durable journal with expiry is SG-000120 work). Records hold paths, sizes, hashes, states and step outcomes, never file content.

App API: `task.list` and `task.get`, which CR-01 reserved, are served read-only from the registry; `task.updated` events carry `run_id` = task id and `step_id`; `capabilities.get` gains a `report.task` row. No app API method can start, approve, commit, stop or change a task.

Local only: `report/*` from a remote-context envelope is refused before any lease, policy or dispatch step. No MCP tool, OAuth scope or tool profile changes; the shapes are recorded as implemented_hidden in the capability parity inventory. One external client's qualification belongs to F4.

Fixtures and tests on Windows, macOS and Linux: synthetic CSV figures with known totals; positive journey; deny once then approve a fresh commit; overwrite refused; out-of-scope names and folders refused; stale source refused; verifier failure on tampered bytes; app API task.get/task.list and events over the real endpoint. Approval paths run in-process on the real LocalApprovalBroker and ledger with the test-only scripted SOFT decider; a real orceld binary run over stdio proves start, preview and every refusal that fails before the broker, and never reaches a platform approval dialog.
exclude: Overwriting, editing, appending to, moving or removing any file; writes outside the task's folder; directory creation.
Binary, Office, PDF or spreadsheet output; the report is UTF-8 text. Reading XLSX or Excel and the confined WI-05 parser path for workspace files belong to the spreadsheet journey (F5).

A durable task journal, crash reconciliation across daemon restarts and resume summaries (RJ-01..RJ-03, proposed grain SG-000120). Within one daemon run an uncertain write is settled only by the verifier, never by a retry.
MCP tools, remote or relay access, model or planner hosting, and any approval minted, reused or relayed outside the existing broker.
Changes to SG-000096 shell, SG-000108 browser, desktop or process authority.

authority_delta.activation: None. This packet authorizes implementing and proving SG-000126; it adds no capability, tool, dependency, listener or authority.
authority_delta.filesystem: Proposed only: after qualification, create-only creation of one UTF-8 report file (at most 256 KiB) per task, inside the task's existing workspace folder, after one SOFT approval bound to its exact bytes; reads of at most eight workspace text files through the existing provider limits.
authority_delta.approval: Unchanged rules: the existing local broker (repaired by #286) decides every commit with exact digest binding, single use and expiry; nothing in the task model mints, caches or reuses approvals.
authority_delta.app_api: Proposed only: two read-only methods (task.get, task.list) and one event kind (task.updated) on the existing CR-01 endpoint and its peer identity; no new endpoint or listener.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed and SG-000108 browser authority is unchanged.

decisions.question: Sequencing
decisions.decision: F2 follows the browser grain; it is not a third parallel grain. Founder mandate of 2026-10-22, as relayed by the orchestrating session: "After the browser grain, progress automatically through the remaining legitimate dependencies, including: F0/F2/F4: authenticated application integration, local report task and Core MVP qualification", and "Respect actual prerequisites." SG-000108 closed canonically (closeout PR #439, merge eebbe11dfe502d36dcc2b520772ef9ec9e7abce0, matrix on #290), so SG-000126 is activated on that main and runs with SG-000096 as the open pair. Its authority (one create-only report write in an existing workspace folder and two read-only app API methods) is disjoint from SG-000096's.

decisions.question: Donor reuse
decisions.decision: BUILD_NEW on Orcel's own qualified primitives: orcel-provider-fs reads and its create-new write path, the LocalApprovalBroker, orcel-policy shape admission and the CR-01 app API. The registry and transplant matrix hold no donor for a minimal kernel task record; the agent-native tool-call journal (T-AN-04) is the RJ-03 resume port and is not needed for a single-run task.

decisions.question: Planner
decisions.decision: A deterministic test planner on orceld's local stdio protocol proves F2, as the roadmap allows. It is the caller only: it reads the observed sources from the start result, computes figures and proposes text. orceld decides scope, staleness, approval and the write.

decisions.question: Task identity
decisions.decision: orceld generates the task id; a caller-supplied id is refused. Ids name one daemon run and are not reused within it. They carry no authority: every commit still needs its own approval.

invariants: orceld remains the only authority: the planner and the app API never decide scope, staleness, approval or writes.
No existing file is ever opened for writing by a report task.
The approval digest binds the exact destination, bytes and source hashes; any change after approval fails closed before the write.
A task is verified only by the independent checker's re-read; a write that returned success is not enough.
Task records and events carry no file content and no secret.
Remote-context report requests never reach policy or dispatch.

acceptance.claim: Activation is authority-neutral on base eebbe11dfe502d36dcc2b520772ef9ec9e7abce0 (main after the SG-000108 closeout #439), cites the founder sequencing record, and imports no code.

Policy admits exactly report/start, report/preview and report/commit with the bounded argument shapes above; other report operations, targets and unknown arguments are refused; commit is SOFT-classed; the parity inventory lists the three shapes as implemented_hidden and no MCP catalog, OAuth or profile file changes.

A deterministic planner observes synthetic CSV sources, previews and commits a report; after one approval the file exists with exactly the approved bytes and the verifier marks the task verified, on all three CI legs.
Denied approval writes nothing and leaves the task open; a fresh commit asks a fresh approval and succeeds; an approval is never reused across commits.
An existing destination (present at preview, created before commit, or created between approval and write) is refused and its bytes are unchanged.

Out-of-scope names (separators, '..', absolute, drive and UNC forms, bad extension, leading dot, overlong) and folders (outside the workspace, a link or junction, missing, a file, replaced after start) are refused before approval.
A source changed, removed or replaced after start makes preview or commit fail as stale with nothing written, and the task stays stale.
The verifier detects tampered bytes, a wrong size and a changed source, and reports a typed postcondition failure.
task.list, task.get and task.updated events over the real CR-01 endpoint report the journey's states and steps without content; no app API method mutates a task.

A real orceld binary over stdio starts and previews a task and refuses overwrite, out-of-scope and stale proposals before any approval, writing nothing; remote-context report requests are refused before policy or dispatch.

review.alibaba_open_code_review: delegation mode per standing founder decision (2026-10-10) with manual review of excluded files
review.security_review: fresh-context security judge per PR; d1-local advisory only

successor_requirements.sg_000120: A durable task journal and crash reconciliation (RJ-01, RJ-02) replace the per-run registry without changing the create-only and verifier rules.
successor_requirements.f4: One external MCP client drives the same kernel operations through a reviewed tool exposure, with its own transcript and qualification.
successor_requirements.f5: Spreadsheet sources (XLSX or Excel) reach the report task only through a qualified read-only parser path.

activation_note: No capability, tool, dependency or authority change in this activation packet. Separate implementation and closeout PRs must qualify their exact heads; activation CI alone proves nothing about the task.

canonical_evidence.slices: #436 activation (merge 9d3d510); #437 kernel report task, independent checker, app API task methods and Control Room conformance (merge 41fcb6e)
open_follow_ups: F4: one external MCP client drives the report operations through a reviewed tool exposure
SG-000120: durable task journal, crash reconciliation and task expiry or cancel
Control Room: assert the client refuses to send task.* until it adopts them (judge nit)
known_residuals: A same-user process that swaps the task folder in the instant between the last check and the create can place the report elsewhere inside the workspace; the checker then ends the task verification_failed and nothing is retried or deleted.
Task records live for one daemon run; 64 unfinished tasks block report/start until restart.

done_when: On Windows, macOS and Linux, a planner turns known figures into one approved, create-only report that the independent checker verifies, with every refusal path proven, task state visible in the app API, and no overwrite, out-of-scope write, remote path or MCP widening.
